newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures close mixed, pork bellies lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures close mixed, pork bellies lower.

text.p: Overall tight numbers of market-ready hogs compounded by weather-reduced marketings lifted nearby CME hog futures at the close but back months slipped on projections for the USDA Hogs and Pigs report, traders said. Pork bellies fell in nervous trade.
Hog futures closed 0.700 cent per lb higher to 0.375 lower with July up most at 82.650 cents. Pork bellies finished mostly 0.850 to 0.225 cent lower with July off 0.825 at 80.675.

Hot, humid weather cut hog marketings and boosted hog prices up to as much as $60 per cwt in some areas. Friday's Cold Storage report was also considered supportive to futures as total pork stocks were lower than many anticipated. July hog futures in turn, surged through its recent high of 82.750 cents and touched off buy stops, they said.

However, trade turned nervous at times, especially in deferred months, as Friday's quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs report drew closer. Some analysts were looking for a fairly large expansion of the hog herd while others see at least a modest increase.

Early analyst estimates on Friday's report put all hogs on U.S. farms as of June 1 at 101.7 to 104 percent of a year earlier. Kept for breeding numbers were ranging from 103 to 106 percent and kept for market 101 to 105 percent.

Spreaders generally bought nearby hogs and sold deferreds based on current cash strength and expected report numbers. The market is expected to remain nervous and prices trade uneven into the report, traders said.
Pork belly futures traded on both sides of previous levels shortly before the close before ending lower on expectations of a bearish CME Out-of-Town Report Tuesday, they said.

Profit taking and selling on expectations for the report turned prices down from early gains but a large buy order by ING buoyed prices shortly before the close. Renewed selling then took the market down sharply to lower ending values, sources added.
The CME out-of-town report showed net in-movement last week versus an out-movement last year, floor sources said.

Early support in futures reflected higher cash belly prices and last Friday's Cold Storage Report which showed frozen pork belly stocks at 55.713 million, only slightly above the record low for May 31 of 54.98 million lbs.
E.D.& F. Man sold July late into stops for ING bought. Refco and locals sold into the close, pit sources said.
